parsed.explanation: The combined regime is tier-1/tier-2 on several axes. Entry screening instructs refusal where documents cast doubt on sex, with possible lifetime fraud ineligibility; the passport regime has stranded trans travelers. Eight governments now advise trans citizens against travel here. In custody, documented federal immigration abuse of trans men (beatings, solitary, sexual abuse, forced labour) is state-perpetrated, and this division bars all transition care for incarcerated people with no taper. The division has no gender-identity non-discrimination law, strict surgical document rules, and a hostile care regime upheld through 2026. Mitigating: no trans-specific criminal offence, functioning courts, gender-identity hate-crime coverage, and no documented violence incident here. Everyday exposure is friction and conditional denial; custody exposure is severe.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 order ends X markers and self-selection; consular cable directs refusal where documents or evidence cast doubt on sex, with possible lifetime fraud ineligibility; trans travelers report passports blocked/confiscated, some stranded abroad.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid until expiry; fraud finding requires four elements, is never automatic, has limited waiver; suit pending in national courts.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy at entry can escalate to secondary inspection, detention, then federal custody where documented abuse occurs.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Trans men in immigration custody report forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse; this division's HB 2009 (July 2026) bars all transition care for incarcerated people with no taper; corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style policies from 2026.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Habeas and court review exist; some comparable care bans blocked by national courts; corrections bureau policies litigated.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry-stage document doubt feeds into federal custody, where care denial and abuse are documented operative practices.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National map: facility bans in 21 state/provinces, criminal trespass in 4, one documented arrest (Mar 2025) with 24h held in men's ward; 6 units extend bans to private settings. Division's own facility rule not documented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 state/provinces plus capital district have no mapped ban; exemptions and refusal-to-depart requirement limit automatic arrest.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A visitor's exposure depends on which unit she is in; national facilities bars apply to federally funded buildings wherever she travels.

care_services.exposure: Division bars Medicaid payment for gender-affirming care at any age, restricts prison care, threatens provider licences; minor-care ban upheld Jan 2026, with a Nov 2026 ballot initiative to extend it; tipline reports suspected violations.
care_services.protection: SAFE Act sunsets 2027; emergency federal orders withdrawn in 2023 after being blocked; some courts enjoined comparable measures.
care_services.interaction: Care denial combines with custody care ban and insurance exclusions; a traveler entering care risks being flagged.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal counterterrorism strategy targets groups 'radically pro-transgender'; DOJ reward memo frames 'radical gender ideology' among violent-extremist viewpoints; 66% of residents support ASAB on documents; division runs tipline on 'gender transition interventions'.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Memo never uses the phrase as a reward criterion; strategy states powers won't target mere disagreement; marriage and employment protections remain.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises outing probability and emboldens discretionary refusals at entry and in services.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division SAFE Act bans hormones/blockers and all surgery for under-18s, upheld unanimously Jan 2026; federal orders direct criminal investigation of teachers facilitating social transition; youth crisis services shut down.
minors_guardians.protection: Youth already in treatment may continue; law sunsets 2027; federal orders partly enjoined; no documented application to visiting minors' own care being denied at entry.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent travelling with a trans minor faces a division that criminalises providers and invites tip-offs, chilling any care sought during the visit.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No dated incident of violence against a trans person in the division is documented; national bias data show persistent hate incidents; only 23 units cover gender identity in bias-crime statutes.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Division hate-crime statutes explicitly cover gender identity; national hate-crimes statute covers gender identity; national sodomy law absent.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Recourse exists but division lacks non-discrimination law, so service refusals have no state remedy.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Division has no gender-identity non-discrimination law; marker-change route requires surgery; licence policy reverted after unspecified incident; unresolved: SAFE sunset, HB 2009 scope, ballot initiative, pending federal litigation.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning courts: hate-crime coverage, national employment ruling, pending suits over passports and orders have produced injunctions.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies work for some claims but do not touch entry refusals or custody practices the state itself runs.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra's register excludes trans visitors without charge. This jurisdiction does not exclude categorically, but adds worse conditional severity: documented custody abuse, care denial in detention, and a lifetime fraud-ineligibility pathway — deeper than exclusion, yet not routine for every visitor, so it sits below 0.35-A's exposure breadth but above its ceiling on severity.

Closest match: routine exposure at checks, documented detention, humiliation and denial of care, thin and slow remedies, inconsistent enforcement, unpredictable escalation. Like Vesskar, prosecutions of visitors are uncommon and no credible execution pathway exists, placing this squarely in the 0.45 zone.

Kestrel Isles has secondary screening and discretionary entry refusal but only administrative consequences. This regime is materially worse: refusal can become permanent fraud ineligibility, and detention leads into documented custody abuse and statutory care denial, so it rates below 0.55.

Meridia trains border staff, guarantees counsel and compensation, and sees brief detention with functioning appeal. This dossier documents the opposite institutional posture at entry and in custody, plus no state non-discrimination law — clearly a tier or more lower than 0.75.

parsed.synthesis: The operative system stacks federal entry screening onto a hostile division. A trans visitor's documents are the tripwire: the 2025 orders and consular cable make mismatched or doubtful sex evidence grounds for refusal and possible lifetime fraud findings, and eight foreign governments now warn their trans citizens. Escalation runs entry doubt → secondary inspection → federal custody, where abuse of trans people is documented and this division independently bars transition care for detainees. Everyday street exposure is moderate — hate-crime coverage and working courts offset the absence of any state non-discrimination law and a documented public majority favouring sex-assigned-at-birth document rules. No trans-specific criminal offence, no documented division violence incident, and partially enjoined federal orders keep this out of the high-risk tiers; the custody and care exposures hold it in Elevated Risk.
